title: Frenkel line of Yukawa fluids within the self-consistent relaxation theory
authors: Ilnaz I. Fairushin, Anatolii V. Mokshin
abstract: For a simple model fluid, the Yukawa fluid, the condition for dynamic crossover, known as the Frenkel line, is defined. The condition is related to the fact that the roton minimum in the dispersion relation of longitudinal acoustic-like excitations exists only when the collective vibrational dynamics of particles dominates in the liquid. Based on the self-consistent relaxation theory for the Yukawa fluid, thermodynamic states are determined in which the roton minimum disappears. The obtained values of the state parameters for the Frenkel line are consistent with the results of studies in which the position of this line on the phase diagram of the Yukawa fluid was determined using molecular dynamics simulations. It is shown that the Frenkel line in this system can be determined directly from the structural characteristic -- the static structure factor. A physical interpretation of the roton minimum frequency for the simple liquids near the Frenkel line is proposed.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the Frenkel line, a dynamic crossover boundary in the phase diagram of the Yukawa fluid, using self-consistent relaxation theory. The authors show that this line, which separates different dynamic regimes, can be determined purely from the static structure factor $S(k)$ by analyzing the longitudinal excitation spectrum. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for characterizing the dynamics of simple, strongly interacting fluids.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the 'Frenkel line,' a dynamic crossover line in the phase diagram of a supercritical fluid, by analyzing the collective vibrational dynamics.
main_result: The authors derive an analytical expression showing that the Frenkel line can be determined directly from the static structure factor $S(k)$, by equating the local maximum and the roton minimum of the longitudinal excitation dispersion relation.
method: The study employs the self-consistent relaxation theory, expanding the dynamic structure factor $S(k, \omega)$ using frequency moment expansions and relating the crossover condition to the equality of two characteristic frequencies.
model_or_system: The physical system modeled is the Yukawa fluid, which is characterized by purely repulsive interparticle interactions, making it a suitable model for supercritical fluids lacking a sharp liquid-vapor transition.
key_observables: The longitudinal collective excitation dispersion relation $\omega_L(k)$, the static structure factor $S(k)$, and the roton minimum frequency $\omega_L^r(k)$ are key observables.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $\Gamma$ and the Debye screening parameter $\kappa$ define the thermodynamic state; the ratio $\Gamma_F/\Gamma_m$ characterizes the line.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes that higher-order time scales in the expansion of the time correlation function are equalized ($ rac{1}{\Delta_4(k)} =  rac{1}{\Delta_5(k)} = \dots$).
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the phase diagram showing both the melting line and the calculated Frenkel line for the Yukawa fluid. Figure 3 shows the dispersion curves $\omega_L(k)$ illustrating the relationship between the roton minimum and the main maximum.
paper_structure: The paper develops the self-consistent relaxation theory to calculate the dynamic structure factor $S(k, \omega)$. It then derives the dispersion relation for longitudinal excitations and establishes the condition $\omega_L^m(k) = \omega_L^r(k)$ that defines the Frenkel line, finally comparing the theoretical result to molecular dynamics simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the theoretical framework of self-consistent relaxation theory and the analysis of collective excitations are highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body quantum systems, such as those studied in quantum gases or strongly correlated materials.

Figure 2. Phase diagram of the Yukawa system [28]. The solid line corresponds to the melting line, and the dashed line indicates the Frenkel line according to Ref. [7]. The circle marks the triple point. In Ref. [7], an empirical correspondence between the melting and Frenkel lines was proposed: ΓF(κ)/Γm(κ) = 0.05.

Figure 3. Dispersion curves of longitudinal collective excitations ωL(k) normalized by the plasma frequency ωp for the Yukawa fluid at different (Γ, κ)-states, calculated using the self-consistent relaxation theory via Eq. (20).

Fig. 3 shows dispersion curves for longitudinal collective excitations in the Yukawa fluid, obtained from Eq. (19) for thermodynamic states with different particle dynamics regimes. One can see that the location of the roton minimum correlates with the main maximum of the static structure factor S(k) (Fig. 3a), i.e., it lies at the boundary of the second Brillouin pseudozone. As expected, at a fixed screening parameter κ, the roton minimum becomes less pronounced with decreasing coupling parameter Γ (Fig. 3b), which corresponds to an increase in temperature (see Eq. (2)).
